author: Kushal
problem: A graph has N1 + N2 vertices: vertices 1 to N1 are all connected to each other, vertices N1+1 to N1+N2 are all connected to each other, and the two groups are not connected. Read N1, N2, M and the M edges, add one edge between the groups, and print the largest possible shortest-path distance between vertex 1 and vertex N1+N2.
bug_description: The BFS always starts from vertex 0 instead of s, so distances from vertex N1+N2 are never computed.

comments.accurate: Takes the farthest BFS distance from vertex 1 and from vertex N1+N2 and joins them with the new edge
comments.wrong_behavior: Adds the farthest distances from two breadth-first searches that both expand from vertex 1, plus the new edge
comments.wrong_location: BFS start vertex verified; check that the distance list is reset between the two searches
